results.description: system-ERTS startup latency + fixed compute loop

budgets.rationale: A gross-regression alarm for the Rust boot median (the six m19 matched rounds read 260.3-261.4 ms at a 1-min load of 0.5-4.5; m17's loaded rounds read 289-546 ms at load 3-92), not an SLO — a shared host can double it without a code change, so the load-robust judgement is the rust/sys ratio row.

Catches a hang or an order-of-magnitude tail regression (the six m19 matched rounds read 261.9-267.6 ms p99; m17 read up to 485 ms, with a single 1702 ms outlier on a heavily loaded A/B round), not an SLO: a boot's p99 is a handful of samples, so this row only notices a gross failure.

budgets.reason: the ratio needs a usable `sys` `startup_ms` p50 measurement and there is none (no `sys` row for this workload in the report); the `rust` side measured 385.8314
budgets.rationale: The load-robust startup judgement: the six m19 matched rounds read 2.51-2.53x (m16 reached 3.79x), so 6x is a regression alarm with headroom above every recorded round — not a target, and deliberately not so tight that ordinary host drift trips it.

budgets.reason: the ratio needs a usable `sys` `startup_ms` p99 measurement and there is none (no `sys` row for this workload in the report); the `rust` side measured 1118.5009
budgets.rationale: The same instrument for the tail; the p99 ratios track the p50 ones (2.35-2.58x across the six m19 matched rounds) because a boot's p99 is a handful of samples, so the same 6x alarm applies — not an SLO for a shared host.

budgets.reason: no `sys` row for `baseline` in this report (that runtime was not selected, or is unsupported here)
budgets.rationale: The oracle's own tail, recorded at 103.5-113.3 ms across the six m19 matched rounds (m17 read 105-153 ms): a host artifact big enough to move the far less load-sensitive `sys` side shows up here too, so it cannot be misread as a Rust regression — and 400 ms is deliberately loose because this row exists to attribute, not to gate.

budgets.reason: no `cowboy` result in this report (the workload is not registered, or was not selected by --workloads)
budgets.rationale: The request-tail budget on the I/O-bound target, recorded at 0.11-0.16 ms p99 while serving ~119-124k req/s through a real Cowboy release across the three m19 external reps (m17's contended pass read 3.03-3.59 ms at ~38k req/s): 5 ms leaves room for a loaded host yet still flags a real latency regression; it reads the summary the cowboy row actually records (`latency_ms` — there is no separate p99 metric) and it is sys-only because the Rust runtime cannot boot an OTP release.

The per-element dispatch budget for the standing per-unit gap, recorded at 18.4-18.7 ns/element across the six m19 matched rounds (the oracle reads 2.30-2.34; m17's loaded rounds read up to 48.2): over a hundred times today's figure, so it is a regression alarm for the engine's dispatch path and not a parity target — the gap itself is `beam_engine`'s to close.

The messaging budget for the two-process send/receive round trip, recorded at 6242-6338 ns/op across the six m19 matched rounds (the oracle reads 1487-1531; m17's worst round read 12450): ~3.2x above today's figure and still ~1.6x above m17's worst, so it is a regression alarm rather than a parity target, and it is not a hard ceiling on a contended host.

budgets.reason: no `gc_bound` result in this report (the workload is not registered, or was not selected by --workloads)
budgets.rationale: The GC-churn budget for allocate-and-abandon, recorded at 59.6k-60.3k ns/op across the six m19 matched rounds (the oracle reads 4.24k-4.27k; m17's worst round read 106k): ~3.3x above today's figure, a regression alarm for a figure whose collection count the row does not claim — not a parity target.

budgets.reason: no `file_io` result in this report (the workload is not registered, or was not selected by --workloads)
budgets.rationale: The file-I/O budget for the write-then-read round trip of a 4096-byte payload, recorded at 97.6k-103.1k ns/op across the six m19 matched rounds (median 98 643) while the oracle reads 133.9k-135.6k — i.e. the Rust runtime is already ~1.36x cheaper on this case, so the limit sits ~2x above the measured figure as a regression alarm for the file path, not a parity target and not a clean cross-runtime ratio.

budgets.reason: no `gc_class` result in this report (the workload is not registered, or was not selected by --workloads)
budgets.rationale: The GC-class budget for the two-process round trip of a ~390-word payload (deliberately above the nursery, so a collection is admitted), recorded at 51.0k-51.4k ns/op across the six m19 matched rounds (median 51 282) against the oracle's 3.19k-3.27k: the limit is ~3.9x the measured figure, a regression alarm for the copy-plus-collect path — the ~15.8x gap itself is the engine's to close, not what this row gates.
